subject: Post-call: feature catalog gap walkthrough & next tests
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@opsco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Holt <jonas.holt@edgeai.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — parity questions

Hi Mina / Marissa —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items so we can scope an apples-to-apples eval:

- Primary asks:
  - Streaming: want to compare p50/p95 token latency and end-to-end delivery behavior (chunk size, partial JSON streaming).
  - Function/tool calling: how Redwood handles deterministic schema enforcement, unknown-field rejection, and multi-tool orchestration.
  - Structured outputs: ability to guarantee strict JSON (no spurious text), and post-parse validation hooks.

- Vendors in scope: Bedrock (Amazon), Vertex AI (Google), Anthropic hosted endpoints, and Redwood hosted API. We want a reproducible harness we can run across endpoints.

- Success signals for OpsCo:
  1) < 200ms p50 streaming latency for 1-2 token increments on 8k context workstreams, p95 under 600ms;
  2) 100% schema-compliant responses for a 200-sample function-calling set;
  3) Clear cost model for tokenized streaming vs non-streaming.

Could you share the parity checklist and an initial test plan? Also confirm whether Redwood supports partial streaming of structured JSON (i.e., emitting object chunks that can be stitched without requiring the full document to be buffered) and how function-calling fallback behaves when a tool schema validation fails.

Appreciate it — happy to loop in infra if you want direct access for load tests.

—Sara
Sara Liu
Senior Product Manager, OpsCo

---

On Fri, 27 Nov 2026 at 11:10 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time today — sending notes and next steps
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@opsco.com>, Jonas Holt <jonas.holt@edgeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 17:30:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + parity checklist (attached)

Sara / Jonas —

Great conversation this morning. TL;DR: Redwood can run the test harness you outlined; primary gaps to validate are streaming granularity and strict schema enforcement when used together with function/tool-calling. Attached is a parity checklist and a short sample prompt set (see attachments).

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Redwood provides a baseline run (hosted API) of the stream vs non-stream flows using your 3 canonical prompts (we'll attach sample prompts in the Drive link).
2) Run the function-calling validation: 200-sample suite that exercises happy path, schema-violation, and ambiguous-instruction cases. We will record success/partial/failure and what fallback behavior triggered (retries, non-conforming output, or error).
3) Side-by-side cost/latency: same prompt+temp/config run across Bedrock, Vertex, Anthropic, and Redwood. We'll use continuous batching disabled for parity, then run again with Redwood optimizations for cost comparison.
4) Deliverables: CSV with p50/p95 latencies, token counts & costs, schema compliance rates, and sample transcripts showing streaming partials.

I attached: 20261128-parity-checklist.xlsx and sample-streaming-prompt.txt. Quick notes on two of your questions:
- Partial streaming of structured JSON: Redwood's streaming path can emit partial tokens of JSON. We recommend the stitcher in your client validate each chunk boundary (we can provide a small client helper). If strict atomic objects are required, we can toggle a chunking policy to emit full object blocks, but that increases end-to-end latency.
- Function-calling fallback: by default Redwood returns an explicit validation error and a structured exception object that indicates which fields failed. Customers can configure an automatic retry with relaxed validation or an immediate tool rejection. We'll include both behaviors in the test matrix.

Please confirm (1) whether you want Redwood to provision temporary API keys for you to run the harness, or (2) have OpsCo run the harness and share results. We recommend option 1 for speed — we'll provision scoped keys and a short-lived test environment.

Proposed timeline: baseline run by 11/30, side-by-side by 12/03, deliverables by 12/06.

cc: Diego + Marissa — can you help with the test harness and pick up the initial run?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
(attachment: 20261128-parity-checklist.xlsx)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + parity checklist (attached)

Mina / Marissa —

Thanks — I sketched an initial harness and notes below. I can own the baseline run if we agree on the config.

Test harness outline (baseline parity run):
- Environment: Redwood hosted single-tenant test node (n1-standard equivalent). Keys: scoped, 72hr TTL.
- Prompts: use sample-streaming-prompt.txt (3 prompts: short chat summary, 1k-token extraction, tool call orchestrator).
- Streaming configuration: chunk_interval=50ms, max_chunk_tokens=8. Also capture chunk boundaries for reassembly.
- Function-calling config: strict_schema=true for run A, strict_schema=false for run B (to measure fallback cost).
- Metrics to capture: request_start, first_token_time, last_token_time, tokens_emitted, response_size, validation_result (pass/partial/fail), error_code, total_cost_usd.
- Comparison runs: Bedrock/Vertex/Anthropic using the same prompts and tokenization settings. We'll use a small wrapper to normalize their streaming semantics into our chunk model (they differ: Bedrock sends chunk deltas, Vertex bundles larger chunks, Anthropic currently doesn't support partial token streaming for function responses).

Open questions for sales:
1) Do we have permission to run Bedrock/Vertex tests from our test account or should OpsCo provision theirs? (Vendor TOS can block cross-tenant benchmarking.)
2) Which latency buckets matter most — our standard p50/p95 p99? I recommend p50/p95 for executive summary plus p99 for SRE sensitivity.

I'll draft the run script and push to the Drive folder; ETA for baseline run (Redwood hosted) is 11/30 EOD PST if nobody flags the config.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
SW Engineer, Inference Platform — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + parity checklist (attached)

Mina —

Thanks, this looks great. OpsCo approves Redwood provisioning temporary keys (option 1) so your team can run the baseline. Please proceed with the baseline run by EOD today as suggested.

Two quick asks:
- Please include p99 latency in the deliverables (we have SRE constraints).
- For function-calling: include at least one test that exercises multi-tool orchestration (call tool A -> transform -> call tool B) and show how Redwood surfaces partial failures.

If you can drop the temporary keys + instructions into the Drive link you shared, we'll unblock infra to observe.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the CSVs.

—Sara
